question: I am writing to the European Commission in relation to the proposed regulations establishing the financial framework and rules for implementing rural, regional and fishing development policy for 2028–2034. The analyses of national and European organisations (including local action groups and LEADER/CLLD structures) that I have seen reveal a wide range of ambiguities and risks related to the proposed solutions.

Firstly, the draft legislation mentions the possibility of exclusively restricting the definition of beneficiaries of the LEADER approach to farmers, threatening the multisectoral nature of local action groups and limiting the participation of local communities, entrepreneurs, nongovernmental organisations and local authorities in the implementation of bottom-up strategies.

Secondly, the articles on CLLD and LEADER are drafted in ambiguous terms, which creates a risk of conflicting interpretations in Member States and a weakening of the bottom-up principle, which has been a core principle of LEADER for over 30 years.

Thirdly, the lack of a minimum guaranteed financial allocation for LEADER/CLLD under the new NRP fund may lead to the marginalisation of this instrument, especially in countries with centralised governance models. In light of the foregoing: 1.
Can the Commission confirm that the beneficiaries of LEADER will remain local actors in the broad sense and not only farmers?
Will the Commission clarify the relationship between CLLD and LEADER in order to avoid double standards and inconsistencies?
Does the Commission intend to introduce a minimum level of funding for LEADER/CLLD under the 2028–2034 MFF?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.2.2026) 1. The Commission confirms that the beneficiaries of the proposed LEADER1 intervention can include a wide range of local actors such as non-governmental organisations, rural businesses, public authorities and other bodies, in line with the Commission’s commitment to preserve vibrant rural areas and make them stronger, more resilient, connected and prosperous2. 2.

LEADER is an example of community-led local development implemented in rural areas. All features of community-led local development apply to LEADER. 3. The Commission proposes an obligation to programme LEADER in all Member States, at least to provide support in rural areas with specific disadvantages.

The financial allocation for LEADER will be proposed by each Member State in its national and regional partnership plan and will be financed from the non-allocated part of the plans. The Commission will provide guidance for the programming of the national and regional partnership plans 2028-34, including Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) national recommendations.
1 https://eu-cap-network.ec.europa.eu/networking/leader_en. 2 A long-term Vision for the EU's Rural Areas - Towards stronger, connected, resilient and prosperous rural
